title: Precipitation
learningObjective: Students will identify different types of precipitation: rain, snow, sleet, and hail

procedure.instruction: View the photo gallery showing different types of precipitation: rain, snow, sleet, and hail.
scaffoldingSupports: Discuss: 'Have you seen rain before? What about snow?'
Point out differences in each type

procedure.instruction: Match weather conditions to precipitation types. Drag each type to the correct temperature.
scaffoldingSupports: Hint: Sleet and hail = very cold

procedure.instruction: Sort pictures: Which ones show precipitation? (fog, dew, rain, steam)
scaffoldingSupports: Remind: Precipitation = water falling from clouds
Fog and dew don't fall from clouds

procedure.instruction: Learn vocabulary: precipitation, rain, snow, sleet, hail.
scaffoldingSupports: Define precipitation: Water that falls from clouds
Show real photos of each type

multimediaResources.caption: View photos of rain, snow, sleet, and hail
multimediaResources.accessibilityDescription: Photo gallery with labeled images of different precipitation types

multimediaResources.caption: Match precipitation to temperature conditions
multimediaResources.accessibilityDescription: Drag and drop matching game for precipitation types

exitTicket.questionText: Draw a picture showing precipitation. Label what type it is (rain, snow, sleet, or hail).
exitTicket.correctAnswer: Any drawing showing water falling from clouds, correctly labeled
exitTicket.explanation: Precipitation is water that falls from clouds. It can be rain (liquid), snow (frozen crystals), sleet (frozen raindrops), or hail (ice balls).
